rationale: ReSBM is a compiler technique for scale and bootstrapping management in RNS-CKKS encrypted inference. Its contribution places cryptographic maintenance operations in an FHE data-flow graph rather than adding or optimizing hardware/software compute kernels.

Pruner accelerates tensor-program schedule search in TVM using draft-then-verify exploration and online adaptation. Tensor-program tuning is compiler/autotuner work whose output is optimized operator kernels for GPUs.

TurboAttention enables quantized attention execution through FlashQ, SAS, and Triton kernel support for INT8 matmuls and low-bit KV cache handling. The work changes attention precision/format and implements kernels to obtain measured latency and throughput gains.

HALO is a loop-aware compiler pass for placing FHE bootstrapping operations and managing ciphertext levels in encrypted programs. Although it improves FHE execution, the contribution is program-level cryptographic operation placement rather than kernel generation or kernel-level scheduling.

The paper presents lossless floating-point compression algorithms with compatible high-throughput CPU and GPU implementations, reaching hundreds of GB/s on GPUs. These compression/decompression routines are compute kernels optimized for CPU/GPU throughput.

Exo 2 is a user-schedulable language that lets users build scheduling libraries from safe primitives. The evaluation uses those libraries to generate and optimize many high-performance kernels across BLAS, image, and accelerator targets.

SampleAttention is a sparse attention acceleration method with runtime key-value filtering and hardware-efficient kernels. It directly reduces attention I/O and computation and is evaluated against FlashAttention2 for long-context LLM prefill.

BQSim is a GPU-accelerated batch quantum circuit simulator that converts decision diagrams into GPU-efficient data structures and uses task-graph execution to reduce kernel launch overhead and overlap data movement. The main contribution is optimized GPU computation for quantum simulation.

The paper explicitly designs optimized software kernels for N:M-pruned convolution and fully connected layers on RISC-V microcontrollers. It also extends a DNN compiler to use those sparse kernels in complete networks.

TASDER maps arbitrary sparse tensors into sequences of structured sparse tensors so unstructured sparse DNNs can run on structured sparse accelerators such as 2:4 tensor cores. This is a low-level tensor layout/dataflow transformation for sparse DNN acceleration.

CMSwitch is a DNN compiler for CIM accelerators that chooses compute-vs-memory array modes and maps/schedules operators with dynamic programming and mixed-integer programming. The contribution is compiler scheduling and operator mapping for DNN execution on accelerators.

MEADOW changes the LLM attention/decoder dataflow with token-parallel head-sequential execution plus weight and bit packing to reduce off-chip memory traffic. The work is a kernel/dataflow-level scheduling and layout optimization for edge LLM inference on FPGA-class hardware.
